value.consequence: The delivered texts support a field-specific standard independent of any proposed question: a substantial advance must supply a structural, quantitative, methodological, or explanatory gain not already supplied by the applicable stability results. Current open status and application-specific priority require separate evidence.
value.reason:
1. Field and documented active lines. The field is extremal graph theory, specifically how proximity to an extremal objective constrains structure. The supplied works document three connected research lines, with activity established through the June 2024 Chen–Liu text, not independently through October 2026. Korándi–Roberts–Scott (KRS), Exact Stability for Turán’s Theorem, determines the near-extremal trade-off between edge count and deletion distance D_r to r-partiteness. Theorem 1.2 supplies a pentagonal Turán graph with at least as many edges and at least as large D_r as any sufficiently dense K_{r+1}-free graph. This domination theorem does not itself classify every equality case. Pikhurko–Sliačan–Tyros (PST), Strong Forms of Stability from Flag Algebra Calculations, develops robust and perfect stability, certificate criteria, local attachment and edge-flip conditions, and determination of optimal blow-up proportions. Chen–Liu (CL), Strong stability from vertex-extendability, develops local-to-global structural forcing for generalized Turán problems. Its Theorem 1.7 states that edge-stability and vertex-extendability imply degree-stability under uniformity, smoothness, local Lipschitz continuity, continuity, and local monotonicity assumptions. The graph applications include pentagon counts in triangle-free graphs and multipartite structure for generalized Turán objectives. These are mathematical connections between research lines, not merely shared terminology.

2. Nearest documented problems and their missing gains. KRS Conjecture 5.1 asks whether, for fixed k ≥ 2, sufficiently small δ, every fixed 0 < δ₀ < δ, and sufficiently large n, each C_{2k−1}-free graph with (1/4−δ)n² ≤ e(G) ≤ (1/4−δ₀)n² is dominated in edge count and D_2 by a C_{2k+1}-blow-up. Beyond its triangle benchmark, a resolution would identify whether longer odd-cycle blow-ups give the exact obstruction to bipartiteness, rather than merely bounds of the right order. The restriction away from the extremal density is substantive: KRS Section 5 gives a C_5-free construction extremely close to extremality that defeats the unrestricted C_7-blow-up proposal. KRS also identifies exact stability for general edge-critical forbidden graphs as a direction where even the appropriate extremizing family is unclear. A definite resolution would identify that family and its deficit regime, or exhibit an obstruction to a proposed description; the known ordinary extremal graph does not determine this trade-off.

CL explicitly asks for the tight ε in Theorem 2.3: sufficiently high minimum C_5-degree in a triangle-free graph forces C_5-colourability. A sharp threshold, with matching non-colourable obstructions, would determine the boundary of local structural forcing that an unspecified positive ε does not determine. KRS also records Erdős’s conjecture D_2(G) ≤ n²/25 for every triangle-free graph. Its resolution would control bipartite deletion distance across all densities, beyond a near-extremal interval; a balanced C_5-blow-up supplies the proposed sharp obstruction. These are documented questions, not certifications of their present open status. Finally, extending certificate or vertex-extension criteria is a meaningful methodological direction only after specifying the missing hypothesis, newly covered class, or precise limitation to be resolved. Automation as an aspiration is not a definite mathematical question.

3. Substantial mathematical advance. Qualifying gains include a sharp deficit–distance law with matching constructions in a genuinely new regime; identification of the configurations responsible for that law; a structural transition between competing obstruction mechanisms; a local-to-global theorem covering cases excluded by existing hypotheses; or a precisely delimited limitation of a named method. Such results would change which configurations specialists examine, which hypotheses they verify, or which explanations they use. A conceptual explanation can itself constitute the gain.

The distance, target family, objective normalization, parameter dependence, and order of limits must be explicit. KRS distinguishes deletion distance to r-partiteness from edit distance to the balanced Turán graph: a constant-size transfer between parts can cause only O(1) edge deficit but Ω(n) distance to the balanced graph. PST likewise exhibits quadratic objective loss versus linear normalized distance under part imbalance. Perfect stability controls edit distance to the entire blow-up family linearly by the finite-n objective deficit, without robust stability’s 1/n floor, and consequently forces sufficiently large exact optimizers into that family. Degree-stability instead uses a minimum local objective contribution to force structural membership. Neither an existential degree-stability theorem nor perfect stability automatically determines the optimal global deficit–distance function. KRS’s progression from qualitative stability through the reported O(t^{3/2}/n) estimate to an exact extremizing family illustrates distinct mathematical gains; it does not make every sharper constant substantial. A constant improvement needs an explanation of its effect, such as identifying a threshold or separating mechanisms.

4. Specialist meanings of levels 2 and 3. On B1 standing, level 2 requires evidence of an active line, a specific unmet need, and a reduction or other mathematical connection fixing the question’s place in it. For example, a proposed missing extension property must be shown to activate a named theorem with its other hypotheses satisfied. The account must explain the substantial advance, answer the strongest objection that existing stability already provides it, and delimit remaining uncertainty. Activity or shared blow-up notation alone is insufficient. B1 level 3 additionally requires a demonstrated or compellingly argued consequential obstacle that resolution removes, and an explanation of why existing theorems and nearby alternatives do not already remove it. A conceptual argument can establish this without a proved downstream implication.

On B2 influence, level 2 requires evidenced mathematical consequences or explanatory distinctions regardless of present activity: a named implication becoming unconditional; a bound–construction gap being closed; competing obstruction mechanisms being distinguished; a limitation of a specified method being established; or a connection between methods or areas being clarified. State what either answer would establish when relevant, why that change matters, and why it is not redundant. Failure of one sufficient criterion is not failure of the entire method: PST’s paw example fails the automatic criterion for its certificate but is handled using other criteria. B2 level 3 additionally requires a compelling account that resolution meets an important unmet need, removes a consequential obstacle, or changes an organizing explanation or connection, with an explicit comparison against existing results. General mentions of counting, random structures, or complexity are not evidence of a particular dependency. On both grounds, established premises need appropriate proofs, decisive readings, or admitted computations; argued significance must meet the strongest objection. The significance grade is the higher supported ground, never their sum.

For comparative priority, level 2 requires comparison of credible alternatives by mathematical payoff, not merely their names: exact versus asymptotic trade-offs, local forcing thresholds versus global deficit laws, distance to a family versus a balanced optimizer, and fixed-density versus vanishing-deficit regimes. Name and answer the strongest relevant objection—known reformulation, automatic corollary, parameter increment without a new mechanism, absence of meaningful gain, or a neighbour with the better payoff. Explanatory significance can answer the objection without further theorems. Level 3 additionally requires a concrete advantage supported by mathematical distinctions. The imbalance examples, KRS’s small-deficit counterexample, and PST’s separation of classical, robust, and perfect stability are documented distinctions that can support such an argument; none automatically establishes priority. A neighbour’s settledness or equivalence alone is insufficient. Level 0 supplies no account; significance level 1 lacks adequate premises or an answer to the strongest objection, while comparative level 1 merely lists neighbours without identifying the strongest case against interest.

5. Uninteresting formulations. Warning cases are a restatement of a known question or result without distinct gain; an arbitrary parameter variant of a settled case; a routine consequence presented as a new structural issue; a conjecture resting on numerical patterns alone; and a programme with no definite resolution condition. Numerical SDP output is not an exact verified certificate. Conversely, absence of a route to progress is not itself disqualifying when the significance case reaches level 3, and absence of downstream consequences is not disqualifying when the explanation is itself substantial. Accessibility describes presentation or prerequisites, not value. Effort, sunk cost, desired outcomes, ordinal ratings, and majority opinion do not establish significance or priority.
